title: 〜がてら
meaning: while doing …; taking the opportunity of …
simpleExplanation: Aがてら B means you do B while doing A, with one outing serving both purposes. A is usually a movement-type activity (散歩, 買い物, 送る) and B is done along the way. The tone is light and everyday: "I'll pop into the bookshop while I'm out walking."
whenUsed: Mostly spoken or light written Japanese (diaries, blogs). Formal letters use かたがた instead. The action is usually a physical outing.
formation: Vます-stem + がてら (歩きがてら, 送りがてら)
Noun of action + がてら (散歩がてら, 買い物がてら)
Aがてら + B: B is the sentence's main verb

rows.label: 〜がてら
cells: 散歩がてら手紙を出す

rows.label: 〜かたがた

rows.label: 〜ついでに

出かけたついでに買う

examples.ja: 散歩がてら、郵便局まで手紙を出しに行った。
examples.reading: さんぽがてら、ゆうびんきょくまでてがみをだしにいった。
examples.en: I went to the post office to mail a letter while taking a walk.
examples.note: Walk (main outing) + mailing a letter (second purpose).

examples.ja: 買い物がてら、新しくできたカフェをのぞいてみよう。
examples.reading: かいものがてら、あたらしくできたカフェをのぞいてみよう。
examples.en: While out shopping, let us have a look at the new cafe.
examples.note: Shopping trip + a peek into a new cafe; volitional ending shows the casual tone.

examples.ja: 駅まで送りがてら、駅前の本屋に寄った。
examples.reading: えきまでおくりがてら、えきまえのほんやによった。
examples.en: While seeing her off to the station, I dropped by the bookstore in front of it.
examples.note: 送りがてら: verb stem + がてら, movement to the station.

examples.ja: 気分転換がてら、近くの公園まで走ってきた。
examples.reading: きぶんてんかんがてら、ちかくのこうえんまではしってきた。
examples.en: I went for a run to the nearby park, partly to refresh myself.
examples.note: がてら works with an abstract purpose too, as long as movement is involved.

examples.ja: 実家に帰りがてら、昔の友人に会ってくるつもりだ。
examples.reading: じっかにかえりがてら、むかしのゆうじんにあってくるつもりだ。
examples.en: While going back to my parents' home, I plan to meet an old friend.
examples.note: Verb stem 帰り + がてら.

similarGrammar.difference: Formal equivalent used in business letters with nouns like お礼 / ご挨拶. がてら is everyday.
Adds an incidental action to a trip already planned; the second action is minor. がてら gives both roughly equal weight.
A long-term second occupation, not a single outing.

commonMistakes.wrong: 散歩するがてら、手紙を出した。
commonMistakes.right: 散歩がてら / 散歩しがてら、手紙を出した。
commonMistakes.why: がてら follows a noun or the ます-stem, not the dictionary form.

commonMistakes.wrong: お礼がてら、部長のお宅に伺いました。
commonMistakes.right: お礼かたがた、部長のお宅に伺いました。
commonMistakes.why: For a formal visit to a superior use かたがた; がてら sounds too casual.

commonMistakes.wrong: テレビを見がてら、宿題をした。
commonMistakes.right: テレビを見ながら、宿題をした。
commonMistakes.why: がてら needs an outing or movement; two simultaneous actions at home take ながら.

usageNotes: Typical first elements: 散歩, 買い物, 見物, 帰省, 運動, 送り, 帰り.
The main verb (B) usually involves going somewhere: 寄る, 行く, 出す, 会う.
It is friendlier than かたがた and more purposeful than ついでに.
jlptTips: Choose がてら when the first action is an everyday outing and the register is casual; choose かたがた when the noun is お礼 / ご挨拶 and the verb is 伺う.
ながら is a distractor: it needs two simultaneous actions in the same place, not an errand on the way.
In 並べ替え the chunk Nがてら typically comes first, followed by the destination and the main verb.
